Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes on hosted API (since 08:45 PDT)

Monica / Redwood team,

Since about 08:45 PDT this morning we've seen a sharp increase in tail latency for our inference calls to the hosted API. p95 is up to ~900ms (normal ~220ms) and p99 is spiking to 2.4s. Error rate climbed from ~0.1% to 1.2% for a 30-minute window. Our throughput is steady; we didn't change traffic.

We've attached a short Datadog screenshot showing the spike and a few sample request IDs. Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side or something in our integration? This is impacting checkout conversions.

Sample traces: request=rc-9a3f, rc-9a8d, rc-9b02
Attachment: datadog_p99_spike.png (image/png)

Thanks,
Oliver

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes on hosted API (since 08:45 PDT)

Folks — quick update from infra: around 08:38 PDT an automated maintenance job that clears stale KV entries ran across a subset of host pools in us-west that service smaller-cold-tenant prefixes. The job incorrectly included a namespace used for prefix warmup cache. Result: large fraction of NimbleCart's prefixes were evicted; initial traffic following eviction hit cold-key paths and caused heavy KV miss penalties and subsequent p95/p99 regressions.

What I found:
- Eviction job ID: maintenance-evict-2027-04-02-0838 (linked in INF-9203)
- Datadog snapshot attached (see INF ticket and the png Oliver sent).
- Error rate bump correlates with retries on the client side; server-side error % did not show mass 5xxs but many requests crossed cold-path latencies.

Immediate mitigations I triggered at 09:10 PDT:
1) Paused the eviction job across the affected pools.
2) Kicked off a targeted prefix rewarm for NimbleCart using warmup helper (velocity 50 concurrent replays).
3) Temporarily raised prefix-cache TTL for the fleet by +4h to avoid re-eviction while we investigate.

Next steps:
- Engineering will produce a hotfix to exclude prefix-warmup namespaces from the eviction job and add a safety flag.
- Ops to run a backfill rewarm job to fully restore steady-state; ETA for full normalization ~2-3 hours from now depending on prefix count.

I'll post traces when the rewarm completes.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Action items we are taking for NimbleCart:
- Full backfill rewarm (in progress).
- Add a dedicated protection flag for your prefixes to be excluded from global evictions.
- Postmortem and a permanent hotfix to INF-9203 with timeline by EOD.
- Offer a one-time service credit for the incident window; Ben will coordinate details.

11:00 PDT quick sync invite sent — joining details in the calendar invite.

Best,

- Prefix-cache TTL +4h on affected pools
- Eviction job disabled for namespace warmup-keys (safety toggle enabled)

Permanent work scheduled:
- Hotfix to eviction operator to check namespace allowlist (deploy target: 2027-04-05).
- Post-incident audit to add more telemetry around prefix eviction impact (INF-9203).

I'll keep monitoring for 24h and will run an additional rewarm during quiet hours to ensure stability.
